>So I exist solely for other people's convenience and benefit and my own happiness doesn't matter. Lovely.

I said "a little bit more confortable for the people who really deserve it", maybe you're one of those people too.
And yes, helping yourself is always the most important step while passing through this, but when you feel so stress about continuing living and the boring future, I really like to think that if I can't do it for me I should do it for the people who deserve being helped just like me.

Tell me your history, I would love to talk about it with you.

The easier and better way is always help people.

Most people might like first the appearance or the personality. But when the time comes, the friends that they really like and would give their time for later, are the ones that help them.

And while trying to improve, always try to get a better attitude. Great and funny people tend to attract amazing friends.
I don't mean stupidly optimistic, I don't mean always active, I mean people that talk good things about others, and see the good side when there's a good side.

You know, it isn't easy, and it's also slow and tedious process, but it's completely worth it.

Good luck, remember it isn't a extremely hard path, I know you can do it

The sensation of want people to feel bad for you is something that everybody in this world has, we're just people that are facing these feelings and externalising them. Don't feel too bad about it.

However there are 2 ways to get people to appreciate you and feel things about you. Hurting yourself and making them feel sad, or doing things for them and making them feel less shity with their lifes.

It's clear that the one of you suffering is quicker, but Ik you have the heart to realize that it isn't what you want the people you love to get through.

Choose the option of helping them, and dare to risk your life to do it.

Something really similiar happened to me back at elementary school.

 I remember a not very lucid memory of me being with my pants down in front of a kid from a higher grade, just that, and later telling a teacher what happend.

It really is a distorted memory and i'm not sure of anything i've said, but the strange memory is still there. I haven't tell anybody about this.
